four_revision_findings_verbatim.manual_witness: In Y, put m=F_d(x). The tagged relation with core coefficient m and membership coefficient -S satisfies m*S-S*m=0. Its unreduced core coefficient is the nonzero element m of Z_J, but its core coefficient modulo J is zero. Thus the unreduced and reduced projections have different kernels before quotienting E. Also F_3(x)=x^3-3*x^2+2*x makes x^3 congruent to 3*x^2-2*x; ordinary homogeneous degree is not preserved.
four_revision_findings_verbatim.objection: Z_J is defined as a submodule of R^r, whereas the stated projection sends core coordinates modulo J, hence lands in (R/J)^r. Quotienting that image by projected E does not define a map to the unquotiented Z_J. The requested degreewise kernel/cokernel consequently has no single specified map. The finite affine membership ideal is inhomogeneous, so reducing modulo it is not a homogeneous degree-preserving map from the primary h-graded slices.

Declare every kernel/cokernel source and target. Separately freeze a graded construction using homogenized memberships and shifted core modules, or explicitly define a filtered affine comparison plus its strictness/degree-completeness obligations. Do not apply finite affine normal-box counts to h-graded modules.
